receipt.public_excerpt: “The intent of the video was not to accurately portray what was available for customers in 2016. It was to portray what was possible to build into the system,”

evidence_items.explanation: Tesla's Autopilot software director testified that the video showed what Tesla aspired to build, not what it had. This supports the 'aspirational, not real' part.

receipt.public_excerpt: Drivers intervened to take control in test runs, he said.

evidence_items.explanation: Test runs needed human takeovers, and one ended in a crash. This supports the claim that the demo was staged rather than routine.

evidence_items.explanation: Under oath, Elluswamy said the published video was one continuous take that was not stitched together, though it took several attempts. This cuts against 'not a single, unedited run'.

receipt.public_excerpt: It’s been long known that this video was edited to remove a part where the car hit a roadside barrier

evidence_items.explanation: A secondary account says the footage was edited. It conflicts with the sworn testimony, so the editing question is still disputed.

unresolved_gaps: Raw footage and production records are not public, so whether the final cut contains material from more than one run cannot be checked directly.
Elluswamy framed his answer as 'my understanding', and other accounts (The Autopian, earlier NYT reporting) say the video was edited.
